transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate your time. I hope I’m not being a bother. 

I guess I'm here because of some... well, some family stress? I don't want to sound like a complainer, I really try my best to keep the peace, but... it's my husband’s sister. She’s been, um, working this whole situation with the family business so she can get control of the money and push me right out of any decisions. 

I know it probably just sounds like petty drama, and everybody else tries to smooth it over, but... I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. I'm sorry to just unload all that on you right away. Am I doing this right? Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
Do you find yourself thinking about your husband's sister and the family business a lot, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Well, I mean... I wouldn't say I obsess over it or anything. I try to stay busy around the house and keep my mind on positive things. I really do. 

But... yes, I suppose it does cross my mind more than I'd like. It's just hard not to notice when someone is being so... deliberate, you know? Like little comments she makes, or how she always manages to be the one talking to the accountant. I try to just smile and let it go, because I don't want to cause trouble for my husband. He works so hard. 

I just... I want to be a supportive wife, and I don't want to seem like I'm just sitting around stewing over things. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like I'm just being paranoid or holding a grudge.
Do you ever find yourself unable to stop thinking about your husband's sister and the family business, even when you try to distract yourself?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say I'm unable to stop. I really hope I didn't give you that impression. I mean, if I put my mind to it, I can absolutely distract myself. 

I'll just, um, go do a load of laundry or start prepping for dinner, and I can focus right on that instead. I know it wouldn't be healthy to just sit around dwelling on her all day, so I make sure I don't do that. I try to be really good about keeping busy and being productive for my husband. 

I'm not... I'm not obsessing over it, I promise. I can definitely put it out of my mind when I need to. It's just normal to be a little concerned when you see things happening right in front of you, right? I hope I'm explaining this okay. I just don't want you to think I'm losing my head over it.
Are you experiencing significant distress because of the situation with your husband's sister and the family business?

Well, um... I wouldn't use the word "distress." That sounds so... dramatic, doesn't it? I really try not to be the kind of person who gets distressed over things. 

I mean, sure, it's a little frustrating sometimes, just seeing what she's doing and feeling like I have to walk on eggshells around the money stuff. But I handle it fine. I just take a deep breath and remind myself that I'm blessed in so many other ways. I don't let it ruin my day or make me cry or anything like that. I want to be a strong partner for my husband, not someone who falls apart over family squabbles. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I'm in significant distress. Just... mildly bothered, maybe? Is it okay that I feel that way? I just don't want to sound like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill.
Are you having trouble sleeping because of your concerns about your husband's sister and the family business?

Oh, no, my sleep is fine. I really don't let things like that keep me up at night. 

I mean, every now and then, I might take a few extra minutes to drift off if my mind is racing a little, but I think that happens to everyone, doesn't it? I just drink a little warm tea or read a chapter of my book, and I'm out like a light. I always make sure I get a good night's rest so I can be up early to make breakfast for my husband. 

I'd hate to be one of those people who tosses and turns and keeps their partner awake just because they're worrying about things they can't control. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm having any trouble sleeping. I'm doing okay with that, aren't I? I hope that's the right answer.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain family gatherings or events because of your husband's sister?

Well, um... I guess I have missed a couple of family get-togethers lately. But it's not like I'm completely avoiding everyone! I just... well, sometimes it's easier to stay home and let my husband go on his own. 

I just don't want to cause any friction, you know? If she's going to be there, I might just quietly bow out. And I do try to keep our financial stuff and our plans a little closer to the vest these days, just so things don't get back to her. But that's just being prudent, isn't it? It's not like I'm hiding away from the world. 

I still go to all my church activities, and I keep the house running just like always. My routines haven't changed at all. I just want to keep the peace, that's all. I hope you don't think I'm being antisocial or anything. It's perfectly normal to just want a little distance from someone who causes trouble, right?
Do you feel like you have to do certain things in a specific way to cope with the stress of your husband's sister and the family business?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't have any strange rituals or anything, if that's what you mean. 

I just... well, I try to stay busy, you know? I make sure the house is tidy, and I like to have dinner ready when my husband gets home. Just normal things that any good wife would do to keep the home peaceful. I don't feel like I *have* to do things a certain way to cope, I just... I like things to be nice and orderly. It helps keep my mind off the silliness with his sister. 

I definitely don't have any weird habits or anything. Just the usual daily chores. That's a good way to handle things, isn't it? Just focusing on taking care of my family? I really hope that sounds normal to you.
Do you feel like you're repeating certain behaviors over and over?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't repeat things over and over like a broken record or anything. 

I mean, I have my routine, like I mentioned. I make the bed, I dust the living room, I prepare the meals... but that's just keeping a nice home, right? It's not like I'm doing the same chore five times in a row or washing my hands until they're raw. I just do what needs to be done once, and then I move on to the next thing. 

I really try to be efficient with my day so I have time to relax before my husband gets home. So, no, I don't feel like I'm stuck repeating anything. That would be a little strange, wouldn't it? I think I'm managing my day-to-day tasks pretty sensibly. Does that make sense to you?
Do you feel a strong need to have things organized or arranged in a very specific way?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I mean, I like things to be neat, of course. What woman doesn't want a tidy home, right? 

But I don't get upset if a pillow is slightly out of place or if the magazines aren't perfectly stacked. I just try to keep a comfortable space for my husband and me. It's not an obsession or anything, I promise. I just do the normal amount of organizing that anyone would do. I don't need everything to be absolutely perfect, just... nice and presentable. 

I think that's pretty typical for someone who takes pride in their home, don't you agree? I hope you don't think I'm too fussy about it.
Are you finding it harder to fulfill your roles as a wife or in other areas of your life because of your concerns about your husband's sister and the family business?

Well... no, I wouldn't say it's hard to fulfill my roles. I'm still doing everything I normally do. I mean, my home is still taken care of, and I'm still very involved with my church activities. I haven't let any of that slip. 

I suppose... well, I have skipped a couple of family get-togethers lately. But that's just because I want to avoid any drama, you know? It's better for everyone if I just stay out of the way when she's going to be there. And I guess I do keep certain plans or... or money matters to myself now. I just don't want anything getting back to his sister and causing a fuss. 

But really, outside of that, everything is completely normal. I'm still managing my usual routines just fine. That's a sensible way to handle a tricky family situation, isn't it? Just keeping the peace? I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my duties or anything, because I really am trying my best.
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things in a specific way to feel right?

Oh, no... no, I don't think so. I mean, I have my opinions on things, just like anyone else, but I don't feel forced to think a certain way just to feel... right, or okay. 

I just try to look at things logically, you know? Like with the family business and his sister... I just think about it in a way that protects us. But it's not some strange compulsion or anything where my thoughts have to be perfectly lined up. I just try to be practical. 

I don't have any weird rules in my head about how I have to think. That would be a bit concerning, wouldn't it? I just try to keep a level head about everything. Does that sound normal to you? I really just try to be as reasonable as I can be.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with friends or engage in hobbies you used to like because of your concerns about your husband's sister and the family business?

Oh, goodness, no. I make sure to stay busy and see my friends. I still keep up with my quilting group, and... well, my choir practice, too. And I'm still going to my GED lessons and doing my senior walks just like I always have. I haven't let any of my own activities drop, I promise. 

Really, the only thing this whole situation has changed is... well, just how much I trust my husband's sister. And, like I mentioned earlier, which family gatherings I feel comfortable going to. I just steer clear of her when I need to, but my own social life is perfectly fine. 

I think it's so important to keep up with your friends and hobbies when you're dealing with family stress, don't you agree? It shows I'm handling things the right way, I hope. I really am trying my best to just live my life and be pleasant.
Do you feel like you have to mentally replay conversations or events related to your husband's sister and the family business?

Oh... no, I don't think I do that. I mean, if she says something a bit pointed, I might think on it for just a moment, just to make sure I didn't misunderstand her. But I certainly don't sit around replaying conversations over and over in my head like a broken record. 

I try my best to just let things go and move on with my day. Dwelling on every little word just causes unnecessary stress, don't you think? I really prefer to be the kind of person who looks forward, not backward. I just want to keep things peaceful. That's the healthiest way to handle it, isn't it? I really try not to let myself get stuck on things.
Are you finding it harder to maintain your relationships with friends or family members outside of the issues with your husband's sister?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's harder to maintain my relationships. I'm very careful about that. I mean... well, I suppose I have skipped a few family get-togethers lately. Just the ones where I know she'll be there, asking questions. It's just easier to avoid the drama, you know? 

And I guess... well, I do keep certain plans and, um, money matters to myself now when I talk to the rest of the family. I just don't want anything getting back to my husband's sister. It's just a little precaution to keep the peace. 

But outside of that, everything is perfectly fine! I still manage all my usual routines, and I'm very involved in my church activities, just like always. I really try not to let this one little issue spoil my connections with everyone else. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just setting a few polite boundaries? I hope you don't think I'm being unreasonable.
Are you finding it harder to work or take care of daily responsibilities because of your concerns about your husband's sister and the family business?

Oh, goodness, no. My daily responsibilities are just fine. I still keep a very tidy house, and my husband always has a hot dinner waiting for him. I haven't let any of my chores slip, I promise you that. 

I mean, like I mentioned just a moment ago, the only real change is... well, just those family get-togethers I've skipped, and being a little more private about our money and our plans so she doesn't hear about them. But that doesn't affect my daily work at all. 

I'm still keeping up with everything I need to do, and I'm still just as involved at church. I make sure I don't let this situation interfere with my responsibilities. That's the responsible way to handle things, don't you think? Just keeping up with your duties and not letting a family disagreement ruin your whole day? I really hope I'm doing the right thing there.
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things over and over to feel right?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't... I don't get stuck on thoughts like that. I mean, sometimes if I have a lot to do, I might run through my grocery list a couple of times just to make sure I haven't forgotten anything, but that's just being organized, right? 

I don't have to think about things over and over just to feel... right, or comfortable. I just do my best to take care of what needs doing and move on. It's perfectly normal to double-check things in your head every now and then, isn't it? I really try to just keep my mind on my daily tasks and not let myself get carried away with things. That's the best way to be, don't you agree?
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things in a specific order to feel comfortable?

Oh, no, definitely not. I don't need things to be in a certain order to feel okay. I mean, I like to have my day planned out, you know, morning chores first and then maybe some errands, but that's just because I like to be efficient. 

If something comes up and my schedule gets a little mixed around, it doesn't bother me or make me feel uncomfortable. I just adjust and keep going. I'm very flexible that way. It's just good sense to have a routine, but not let it control you, right? I'm sure you hear that from a lot of people, just wanting to keep their day structured?
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with your husband or connect with him because of your concerns about his sister and the family business?

Oh, no, not at all. My husband and I are just fine. We still have our quiet evenings together, and I make sure we have time just for us. I would never let anything come between us, especially not this business with his sister. 

I mean, maybe I'm a little more careful about what I say when we talk about the future, just because I don't want to upset him or... or make him feel caught in the middle. But we still enjoy each other's company just as much as we always have. 

It's so important to keep your marriage strong, even when there's family stress, isn't it? I really try my best to be a good, supportive wife to him, no matter what else is going on. I hope that sounds like the right way to handle it?
Do you feel like you're thinking about your husband's sister and the family business even when you don't want to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's like that. I don't let it take over my mind or anything. I mean, sure, it crosses my mind sometimes because... well, it's an important family matter, and you have to be aware of what's going on. But I don't sit around dwelling on it when I shouldn't be. 

If I'm folding laundry or watching a show, I'm just focused on that. I can put it right out of my head when I want to. It's perfectly normal to think about family issues every now and then, isn't it? I really try to just stay positive and not let things get to me. I think I handle it pretty well, don't you?
Are you finding it harder to maintain your relationships or fulfill your responsibilities outside of the family business situation?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I still do everything I'm supposed to do. I mean, I still keep up with my quilting group, and choir practice... and I'm still doing my GED lessons, which is really important to me. Oh, and my senior walks! I haven't missed a single one. 

I really try to keep my life as normal as possible. The only thing that's really changed is... well, maybe how much I trust his sister, and which family gatherings I feel comfortable going to now. But outside of that, I'm still keeping up with everything else. I think it's important to stay active and keep your commitments, don't you? I really try to be responsible that way.
